answer: Stop sybils with a basalt jetty ivory: an agent stakes a bond for one basalt jetty. Each cycle it sets an ivory tide-mark at the jetty mouth; verifiers read the mark at each tide, voiding a jetty whose mark is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 jetties at 16x cost each: each mark fits one jetty and one tide, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents moor once and keep rights.
